## Overview

The Directory Provider loads every configuration file in a directory, or every file
matching a glob pattern, and merges them into a single configuration. It is used through
the existing `--config` flag, so it composes with other `--config` entries.

## Usage

The scheme for this provider is `dir`. The value after `dir:` is a directory path or a
glob pattern:

```text
dir:/etc/otelcol/config.d          # every *.yaml / *.yml directly in the directory
dir:/etc/otelcol/config.d/*.yaml   # single-level glob
dir:/etc/otelcol/config.d/**/*.yaml # recursive glob — files in subdirectories only
dir:/etc/otelcol/base.yaml         # a single .yaml file (must have .yaml or .yml extension)
```

Matched files are merged in lexicographical order of their paths. Merge semantics match
the rest of the Collector, including the `confmap.enableMergeAppendOption` feature gate.
If no files match, resolution fails with an error.

**Recursive glob note:** `dir:/path/**/*.yaml` matches files in subdirectories of `/path/`
but not files directly in `/path/` itself. This matches common shell globstar semantics
where `**` requires at least one intermediate directory component.

**Single-file note:** a bare path with no glob metacharacters that points to a file (not a
directory) is loaded directly. The file must have a `.yaml` or `.yml` extension.

Example combining a base file with a drop-in directory:

```text
--config=file:/etc/otelcol/base.yaml --config=dir:/etc/otelcol/config.d
```
